'''Sidney David Drell''' (September 13, 1926 &ndash; December 21, 2016) was an American [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]]<ref name="Jaffe"/> and [[arms control]] expert.<ref name="Kubota"/>

At the time of his death, he was [[professor|professor emeritus]] at the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] (SLAC) and senior fellow at [[Stanford University]]'s [[Hoover Institution]]. Drell was a noted contributor in the fields of [[quantum electrodynamics]] and high-energy [[particle physics]]. The [[Drell–Yan process]], which was used to discover the [[Higgs boson]], is partially named for him.<ref name="Jaffe">{{cite journal |last1=Jaffe |first1=Robert |last2=Jeanloz |first2=Raymond |title=Sidney David Drell (September 13, 1926–December 21, 2016): A Biographical Memoir |journal=Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science |date=19 October 2019 |volume=69 |issue=1 |pages=1–14 |doi=10.1146/annurev-nucl-020619-120837 |bibcode=2019ARNPS..69....1J |s2cid=209945149 |language=en |issn=0163-8998|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Biography==
Drell's parents immigrated to America from Ukraine<ref name="Jaffe"/> early in the twentieth century and both went on to obtain college degrees. Born in [[Atlantic City, New Jersey]] on September 13, 1926,<ref name="Jaffe"/> Drell graduated from [[Atlantic City High School]] in 1943, at the age of sixteen.<ref name="Grimes"/><ref>{{cite web| publisher=[[American Institute of Physics]]| author=Aaserud, Finn|authorlink= Finn Aesrud| url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/4578| date=July 1, 1986| title=Oral histories: Sidney Drell| accessdate=2022-02-02}}</ref>

Drell entered Princeton for the summer term in July 1943, and worked with [[Josef-Maria Jauch]] in his junior year and completing his senior thesis "Radiating Electrons" with [[John Archibald Wheeler]].<ref name="Jaffe"/> He earned his undergraduate degree in physics from [[Princeton University]] in 1946.<ref name="Grimes">{{cite news |last1=Grimes |first1=William |title=Sidney Drell, Who Advised Presidents on Nuclear Weapons, Dies at 90 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/12/22/science/sidney-drell-dead.html |access-date=28 March 2023 |work=The New York Times |date=23 December 2016}}</ref> He was awarded a masters in physics in 1947 and received his PhD from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] in 1949.  He co-authored the textbooks ''Relativistic Quantum Mechanics'' and ''Relativistic Quantum Fields'' with [[James Bjorken]].<ref name="Jaffe"/>

Drell was active as a scientific advisor to the [[Federal Government of the United States|U.S. government]], and was a founding member of the [[JASON (advisory group)|JASON Defense Advisory Group]].<ref name="Jaffe"/>
He was also on the board of directors of [[Los Alamos National Security]], the company that operates the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Los Alamos National Security, LLC Announces Board of Governors |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/press-releases/2006-01-19/los-alamos-national-security-llc-announces-board-of-governors |website=Bloomberg.com |access-date=28 March 2023 |language=en |date=19 January 2006}}</ref> He was an expert in the field of nuclear arms control and cofounder of the Center for International Security and Arms Control, now the Center for International Security and Cooperation. He was a Senior Fellow at Stanford's [[Hoover Institution]] and a trustee Emeritus at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton, New Jersey.<ref name="LLNL">{{cite web |title=Drell awarded NNSA Administrator's Gold Medal of Excellence {{!}} Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory |url=https://www.llnl.gov/news/drell-awarded-nnsa-administrators-gold-medal-excellence |website=LLNL Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory |access-date=28 March 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

In early 1970s, Drell (together with [[Tung-Mow Yan]]) did theoretical calculations of lepton pair production in hadronic collisions ([[Drell–Yan process]]), which became an important way to study the parton structure of hadrons. 

He was the father of [[Persis Drell]], former head of SLAC national accelerator lab, former dean of the [[Stanford University School of Engineering]], and (through Fall 2023) provost of Stanford University; Joanna Drell, Professor of History and chair of the Department of History at the [[University of Richmond]];<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://history.richmond.edu/faculty/jdrell/|title = Joanna Drell - History - University of Richmond}}</ref> and Daniel Drell, a program officer at the U.S. Department of Energy. Sidney Drell died in December 2016 at his home in Palo Alto, California at the age of 90.<ref name="Kubota">{{cite news |last1=Kubota |first1=Taylor |title=Sidney Drell, theoretical physicist and national security expert at Stanford, dies at 90 |url=http://news.stanford.edu/2016/12/22/sidney-drell-theoretical-physicist-national-security-expert-stanford-dies-90/ |access-date=28 March 2023 |work=Stanford News |date=22 December 2016 |language=en}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* Member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] (1969)<ref name=NAS>{{cite web|title=Drell, Sidney D.|url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/292547730?pg=vprof&mbr=1006095|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120324090943/http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/292547730?pg=vprof&mbr=1006095|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 24, 2012|work=National Academy of Sciences|access-date=June 3, 2011}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1971)<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780–2010: Chapter D|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterD.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=June 3, 2011}}</ref>
* Member of the [[American Philosophical Society]] (1987)<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Member History |url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Sidney+Drell&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref>
* The 11th Annual [[Heinz Award]] in Public Policy<ref>[http://heinzawards.net/recipients/sidney-drell The Heinz Awards, Sidney Drell profile]</ref>
* [[Enrico Fermi Award]], 2000
* [[National Intelligence Distinguished Service Medal]], 2001
* [[National Medal of Science]], 2011 (presented by President [[Barack Obama]] on February 1, 2013)
